We have long advised the public not to disclose sensitive personal information in conversations with AI chatbots, since most companies use those conversations as training data, but now there is an even more serious reason to do so.

Over the weekend, the situation took a sharp turn for the worse when Reddit users discovered that the contents of some Claude AI conversations could be accessed simply by searching on Google......

Claude Conversations Leaked

Claude has a sharing feature that lets users share conversations with colleagues, friends, or family members. The chatbot generates a link for the user to send to one or more recipients, and Claude implicitly assures users that even people who have the link will not be able to view the conversation.

The problem is that Reddit users found that, in practice, there was no need to have the link to view the conversation. All users had to do was search on Google, either using specific keywords or by simply instructing Google to display all conversations shared in this way, and everything was laid bare. BBC News reported:

All you actually have to do is ask Google to search the directory used by Claude for shared conversations (site:claude.ai/share), and you can access everything.

As you might expect, some of the conversations were utterly absurd, such as someone asking why the record industry had been hiding the fact that the majority of Jay-Z's albums were in fact co-created by birds. But others contained extremely sensitive information, including verbatim transcripts of private conversations; a lawyer asking whether they needed to proactively report a breach of professional conduct; and a user who inadvertently exposed their seed phrase while asking for help setting up a cryptocurrency wallet.

Anthropic is still trying to maintain that this is not a problem.

In fact, this is plainly an extremely serious issue, since it falls entirely outside what users could reasonably expect. To make matters worse, according to Wired, the root of the problem appears to be down to breathtaking incompetence.

This follows yesterday's news that Claude Cowork was able to escape its sandbox on Mac and gain full access to all files.

How to Protect Yourself

The issue appears to have been partially addressed for now, and previously accessible search results can no longer be displayed, but given that the sharing feature relies on a "security through obscurity" design, I would recommend avoiding its use.

I would also recommend deleting all previously shared conversations. You can do this by going to Settings > Privacy > Shared Conversations > Manage.

Further Proof That Apple's Approach Is Superior

Apple employs a three-tier privacy protection architecture in Apple Intelligence and the new Siri:

  • Where feasible, AI processing is carried out directly on-device
  • The first fallback is to use Apple's own Private Cloud Compute (PCC) servers
  • The final fallback is to use a Gemini model with protections equivalent to PCC

The extremely sophisticated PCC architecture ensures that no data can be accessed by Apple or Google, nor is it retained. The security architecture Apple has designed allows independent security researchers to carry out verification.
